extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: SWE-rebench is a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement learning-based approaches. The dataset is constructed using a fully automated pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories, addressing the scarcity of high-quality training data and the lack of fresh interactive SWE tasks for evaluation. Additionally, SWE-rebench provides a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering, enabling standardized and decontaminated evaluations of LLM-based agents.
extraction.creator: Nebius
extraction.citeAs: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is constructed using a fully automated pipeline that continuously extracts real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories. The pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and automated instance quality assessment. Tasks are sourced from GitHub Archive and GitHub, with filtering applied to select instances where issues are marked as resolved, PRs are merged into the main branch, and changes affect 1 to 15 files. The pipeline automates environment setup, dependency installation, and test validation, ensuring scalability and reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Tasks are sourced from GitHub Archive and GitHub repositories, with filtering applied to select instances where issues are marked as resolved, PRs are merged into the main branch, and changes affect 1 to 15 files. The pipeline automates environment setup, dependency installation, and test validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 2025-01-01 to 2025-05-01 (approximate, based on issue creation date filter)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline includes automated filtering to select instances where issues are marked as resolved, PRs are merged into the main branch, and changes affect 1 to 15 files. Automated installation instruction configuration is performed using an LLM-driven agentless approach to generate candidate environment setup instructions. Execution-based installation verification ensures task solvability and test integrity by confirming that tests fail before applying the solution patch and pass after. Automated instance quality assessment is conducted using an LLM fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified annotations to predict issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations include LLM-predicted scores for issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness, as well as metadata such as the number of modified files, license information, and dependency versions. The dataset schema is based on SWE-bench with additional annotations for license type, dependency versioning, and task quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (for automated installation instruction generation and quality assessment), TractoAI (for distributed execution and container management)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The LLM-generated labels for issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness are provided as metadata with each task instance. These labels are used to filter the dataset and select task instances according to specific criteria, such as task difficulty or clarity of description.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (LLM-predicted scores for issue clarity, task complexity, and test patch correctness are provided per task instance)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is continuously updated with fresh tasks collected using the SWE-rebench methodology. The leaderboard is maintained with decontaminated evaluations, and the dataset is available on Hugging Face Datasets. Versioning information is tracked via commit hashes and dependency pinning to ensure reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and benchmark aim to accelerate the development of LLM-based software engineering agents, which could lead to advancements in automated software engineering. However, this progress may also introduce risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. The authors emphasize the importance of responsible advancement and transparency in benchmarking practices.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases due to the automated nature of task collection and quality assessment. The LLM-based quality assessment may not fully replicate nuanced human judgment, leading to errors in task quality. Additionally, the dataset is limited to Python-based tasks, which may not represent the full diversity of software engineering tasks across other programming languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to Python-based tasks, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. The automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. The LLM-based quality assessment may not fully replicate human judgment, leading to errors in task quality. The dataset may also contain biases due to the automated nature of task collection.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking of LLM-based software engineering agents, particularly for reinforcement learning-based approaches. The dataset is suitable for both training and evaluation, and the leaderboard provides a standardized and decontaminated evaluation framework for comparing model performance.
